# Proposed architecture decision

**Status: Proposed — project acceptance required.**

Engine 0.8.0; catalog 0.4.0; services 0.8.0; analysis 0.2.0.
Input SHA-256: 54ac28250ad51d88b1b91478c6399f3ae65cf232e7e703372c0e45ea55ecbf79.

## Original result

PROVISIONAL STACK — unresolved critical constraints require review before production\. modular\_monolith recommendation selected from 21 complete compatible plans; month\-12 infrastructure planning band USD 367\.76–1193\.62/month\.
Result: ok_with_warnings.

- frontend: Next\.js \+ React Native — Covers requested targets android, web with ssr rendering\. Team languages: javascript, python, typescript\. Selected after supporting\-service compatibility and whole\-plan infrastructure cost scoring\. Explicit critical warnings identify provisional data\-flow/control exceptions\.
- backend: Django — Provides a python application runtime for the marketplace profile\. Language familiarity and delivery complexity were compared across compatible whole plans\. Selected after supporting\-service compatibility and whole\-plan infrastructure cost scoring\. Explicit critical warnings identify provisional data\-flow/control exceptions\.
- database: PostgreSQL — relational persistence via Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL\.  Database drivers and host deployment were checked as a combination\. Selected after supporting\-service compatibility and whole\-plan infrastructure cost scoring\. Explicit critical warnings identify provisional data\-flow/control exceptions\.
- hosting: Google Cloud Run — Matches managed\_cloud with provider gcp; reviewed primary compute region asia\-south1\. Required runtimes and separate database deployment were checked\. Selected after supporting\-service compatibility and whole\-plan infrastructure cost scoring\. Explicit critical warnings identify provisional data\-flow/control exceptions\.

Monthly infrastructure/operations band (activity fees additional): USD 367.76–1193.62.

## Complete alternatives

- modular\_monolith\|next\-native\|django\|pg\|cloudrun\|asia\-south1; score 65; USD 367.76–1193.62; selected.
- modular\_monolith\|next\-native\|fastapi\|pg\|cloudrun\|asia\-south1; score 65; USD 367.76–1193.62; alternative.
- modular\_monolith\|next\-native\|fastify\|pg\|cloudrun\|asia\-south1; score 65; USD 367.76–1193.62; alternative.

## Preference stability

Original winner retained in 25/25 tested settings; 1 observed winners. Counts are not confidence probabilities.

## Cost assumptions

- Horizon: expected month\-12 footprint; 730 hours/month\. No tax, development/on\-call labor, domain registration or new on\-prem hardware procurement is included\.
- Peak concurrency supplied: 800; not equated directly with requests/second\.
- RPS absent: assumed 50 requests/user/day averaged across the day \(17\.361 RPS\); peak capacity still uses the concurrency hypothesis\.
- Data volume 50 GB supplied; egress 300 GB/month assumed at 0\.01 GB per year\-12 user, minimum 1 GB; backup retention 1 months assumed\.
- Cloud Run billing separates 3 request\-driven allocations from 3 always\-on reference allocations \(support footprint rounded up\)\. Identity/background workers/inference/telemetry use instance\-based CPU with minimum instances and are charged for the full month; they do not inherit a request\-only duty discount\. Service packing, startup, concurrency and exact regional billing require validation\.
- Compute provisioning hypothesis: 50 RPS or 500 active users per reference allocation; WebSocket capacity is included in the peak\-concurrency replica floor, not charged again as per\-connection sidecars\. 5\.5 vCPU/2\-GiB\-equivalent units include frontend/backend, auth, workers, inference and telemetry once\. These are sizing assumptions requiring load tests, not capacity guarantees\.
- Billed duty 0\.25–1; run polling workers with allocated CPU/minimum instances\. Higher availability adds at least two application allocations and in\-region database copies, but does not guarantee an SLA\. Rate bands include headroom; do not interpret reference regions/proxies as exact local provider quotes\.
- Managed database: 1 vCPU/4 GiB reference primary and 1 failover copies in\-region; no SLA is guaranteed\. Auth/search/outbox share logical database capacity and are not billed as duplicate databases\.
- OTP volume unknown, assumed range 0 to twice the year\-12 users: upper 60000 messages/month\. SMS rate is an explicit unquoted planning envelope; DLT, taxes and country routing may add fees\.
- Payment assumptions: 0–600 transactions/month, average USD 50; missing count assumes up to 2% of year\-12 users and missing ticket assumes USD 50\. Percentage/fixed rates are declared envelopes, not verified merchant pricing\. Payout, FX, tax, refunds and chargebacks require separate quotes\.
- Headline estimate and budget fit cover infrastructure/operations only\. Payment and SMS activity fees are separately itemized scenarios and excluded from this total; missing volumes are assumptions, not measured expenditure\.
- 1 vCPU and 2 GiB active reference rate; upper adds 80% region/SKU/variance allowance; not a current region\-specific quote\.
- Assumed USD/SMS planning envelope only; verify country, tax, DLT and provider quote\. No currency conversion or MSG91 tariff is claimed\.
- Authored backup\-storage envelope with retained copy quantity; no cross\-region copy assumed\.
- Authored hosted build\-minute allowance, assuming included quota at the lower bound\. Paid runners/minutes/artifacts require a repository\-specific quote and spending cap\.
- Authored internet\-egress envelope; actual destination, free quota and routes vary\.
- Authored logs/metrics/request\-operations allowance; redact data and set regional retention/quotas\.
- Authored regional persistent\-storage envelope, including replica copies explicitly in quantity\.
- Authored standard\-storage envelope; requests/lifecycle operations have a separate allowance\.
- Cloud SQL memory reference; a declared proxy for other managed providers, not their quoted rate\.
- Cloud SQL reference CPU with up to 2x geography/SKU allowance; other providers use this declared proxy pending exact quotes\.
- Illustrative 2–3% platform\-fee scenario from the domestic pricing starting point; not a merchant quote\. GST, premium methods, payouts and FX are excluded; no INR/USD conversion is inferred\.
- Iowa on\-demand instance\-based reference: \(USD 0\.000018/vCPU\-second \+ 2 GiB × USD 0\.000002/GiB\-second\) × 3600 = USD 0\.0792/hour\. Upper is an authored 80% geography/SKU allowance, not a regional quote; no free tier or commitment discount applied\.
- No separate fixed per\-transaction fee modeled for standard domestic checkout; other merchant/product/settlement fees require a quote and are excluded, not assumed universally free\.

## Blockers, validation and owner actions

- critical: MSG91 OTP is proposed provisionally: end\-to\-end india data residency is NOT established\. Verify tenant/merchant eligibility, processing, logs, backups, delivery partners and contracts before production\. This warning is an explicit exception to verified residency, not approval\.
- critical: Razorpay Checkout is proposed provisionally: end\-to\-end india data residency is NOT established\. Verify tenant/merchant eligibility, processing, logs, backups, delivery partners and contracts before production\. This warning is an explicit exception to verified residency, not approval\.
- warning: 99\.9% is a target, not a product guarantee\. The cost model provisions redundancy assumptions; service terms, failover and workload behavior still require verification\.
- warning: Infrastructure estimate USD 367\.76–1193\.62/month exceeds the USD 150 budget at the lower bound; this is an explicitly over\-budget plan, with no requirement silently relaxed\.
- warning: The output proposes technical control designs only\. It does not certify compliance, establish legal applicability, execute contracts, or replace an audit\. Implement controls and obtain scope\-specific review\.
- warning: No measured evidence establishes the 500 ms p95 target; load\-test the complete client/network/data path\.
- warning: Planning bands combine published reference rates and explicitly authored allowances; they are not regional provider quotes or measured workload capacity\. Validate sizing, merchant/SMS eligibility, storage, requests and current tariffs before purchase\.
- infrastructure\.data\_residency, requirements\.auth: Request the scoped vendor data\-flow and configuration evidence\. Review a regional alternative without changing the original residency requirement\.
- infrastructure\.data\_residency, requirements\.payments: Request the scoped vendor data\-flow and configuration evidence\. Review a regional alternative without changing the original residency requirement\.

- services:msg91\-privacy: [MSG91 privacy](https://msg91.com/privacy-policy); checked 2026\-11\-13; Multiple hosting geographies; strict residency not established by this source\.
- services:pg\-fts: [PostgreSQL full\-text](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/textsearch.html); checked 2026\-11\-13; Native text search; workload suitability must be tested\.

- services:razorpay\-pricing: [Razorpay pricing](https://razorpay.com/pricing/); checked 2026\-11\-14; Published domestic pricing starting point; payment mix, GST, payouts and merchant terms require an exact quote\. No USD conversion assumed\.
- services:razorpay\-privacy: [Razorpay privacy policy](https://razorpay.com/privacy-policy/); checked 2026\-11\-13; Candidate regional payment provider privacy terms; not sufficient to approve every merchant, payment product or international data flow\. Not selected by this release\.
- services:run\-price: [Cloud Run pricing](https://cloud.google.com/run/pricing); checked 2026\-11\-15; On\-demand Iowa request\-based and instance\-based CPU/memory references\. Region/SKU bands remain authored allowances; no regional quote, commitment discount, free\-tier or production capacity guarantee\.
- services:s3\-price: [S3 pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/s3/pricing/); checked 2026\-11\-13; Storage, requests and egress vary; cross\-provider estimate below is a planning envelope\.

## Limits and acceptance

- Exploratory analysis only. The original recommendation and original requirements are unchanged.
- Priority stability counts a finite one-at-a-time sweep; it is not a probability, confidence score or exhaustive sensitivity analysis.
- The tradeoff front covers all complete candidates in this finite reviewed catalog, minimizing cost upper bound and operated components while maximizing the ORIGINAL-priority heuristic score. It does not establish real-world optimality or measured architecture quality.
- Functional experiments try eligible single/pair edits only: phone login to email/password, payments off, offline support off, full-text search off, or unsupported ML off. They are changed projects, never solutions satisfying the original brief.
- Within Decision Lab functional experiments, compliance, infrastructure/residency/provider, tenant isolation, availability, budget, team and timeline are never relaxed. A usable hypothetical result is not legal, security or production approval.
- No user assertion authenticates vendor/tenant evidence. Missing contracts, capacity calibration and independent review remain unresolved.
- engine_evaluations counts top-level scenario trials; the baseline recommendation may additionally evaluate one separately labeled budget proposal. Budget proposals are outside the functional-experiment sweep and never change the baseline brief.
- The generated ADR is Proposed; no stakeholder acceptance, implementation or deployment is inferred.

score_breakdown.reason: USD 367.76–1193.62/month versus budget 150: fit 5 when upper bound fits, 3 when only lower fits, 1 within twice budget, otherwise 0. All selected services are included under disclosed assumptions.
Language familiarity 5.00/5 and implementation-complexity rubric 3.00/5; short delivery/beginner-complexity and manual Markdown-conversion penalties are explicit heuristics.
Static delivery avoids application writes; embedded-writer and growth triggers are ordinal review heuristics, not published capacity limits.
No latency SLA or measured framework throughput is credited; embedded-write concurrency is a review heuristic. Low-memory clients require measurement, not an assumed framework benchmark.
Operational burden 1/5+; no existing-system reuse bonus. Fewer self-operated systems are favored without DevOps. Additional service operating penalty 0.
Baseline configured controls: 3; explicit reviewed tenant isolation: 4. No certification/audit credit is assigned.

alternatives.why_not: A compatible plan tied on score; the published cost-upper-bound/operated-component/identifier tie-break selected the primary plan, not intrinsic product superiority.

backend.justification: Provides a python application runtime for the marketplace profile. Language familiarity and delivery complexity were compared across compatible whole plans. Selected after supporting-service compatibility and whole-plan infrastructure cost scoring. Explicit critical warnings identify provisional data-flow/control exceptions.
tradeoffs: Business features, authentication and compatible database drivers must be configured; the framework alone is not the application.

tradeoffs: Data model, backup policy, licensing and release/driver compatibility need explicit review.

tradeoffs: Client accessibility, security and device behavior still require implementation and testing.

tradeoffs: No workload pricing/SLA is inferred; region, storage, backups, identity and networking require deployment review.

tradeoffs: Source and synthetic fixtures only; production data, secrets and personal data must never be sent to external build logs. Usage above included minutes is billed.

alternatives.why_not: More custom integration/operation than this reviewed option.

tradeoffs: Choose the same reviewed region, private access, signed URLs and in-region lifecycle/backup policy; do not use a default multi-region bucket.

alternatives.why_not: More custom integration/operation than this reviewed option.

supporting.justification: Authentication method phone_otp uses a separate Keycloak realm/schema and least-privilege database identity. Deploy in the same reviewed compute/data region; explicit configuration is required.
tradeoffs: Separate realm/schema and restricted database credentials are required; pin supported driver/database versions. Email delivery needs a separately reviewed SMTP integration if enabled.

alternatives.why_not: More custom integration/operation than this reviewed option.

supporting.justification: Phone delivery uses a provider OTP API; integrate a custom Keycloak authentication SPI rather than mislabeling TOTP as SMS.
tradeoffs: Regional API/Indian company status is not proof all data stays in India; DLT rules, contracts, fees and delivery need verification.

alternatives.why_not: More custom integration/operation than this reviewed option.

supporting.justification: Collect redacted metrics/logs/traces with regional retention; on cloud use a configured host-provider regional log bucket, locally use provisioned persistent storage. Deploy in the same reviewed compute/data region; explicit configuration is required.
tradeoffs: Redact sensitive values, use host-region retention/routing, and provision a durable regional log backend. No personal data in tracing baggage.

alternatives.why_not: More custom integration/operation than this reviewed option.

supporting.justification: Application and outbox writes commit atomically; a separately budgeted worker retries idempotently and records dead letters.
tradeoffs: Outbox rows share the database bill. Worker retries must be idempotent; tune polling, retry/dead-letter policy and retention.

alternatives.why_not: More custom integration/operation than this reviewed option.

supporting.justification: Use reviewed database-native search before adding another operated search cluster.
tradeoffs: Indexing, tokenization and language/ranking quality must be tested; not a replacement for advanced search workloads.

alternatives.why_not: India payment/UPI integration is proposed through Razorpay; Stripe merchant eligibility and data-flow scope require separate review.

supporting.justification: Hosted checkout keeps raw payment credentials outside the application; verify webhook signatures, idempotency and merchant scope.
tradeoffs: Merchant onboarding, product eligibility, signed webhooks, idempotency, refunds/payouts and PCI scope require implementation. India-only end-to-end payment flows are not established by the vendor name.

alternatives.why_not: More custom integration/operation than this reviewed option.

supporting.justification: WebSocket transport provides live updates; enforce authorization, reconnects, shared state and backpressure. Deploy in the same reviewed compute/data region; explicit configuration is required.
tradeoffs: Node sidecar with browser/native WebSocket clients; authentication, reconnect/backpressure and fan-out are custom integration work.

Infrastructure estimate USD 367.76–1193.62/month exceeds the USD 150 budget at the lower bound; this is an explicitly over-budget plan, with no requirement silently relaxed.

The output proposes technical control designs only. It does not certify compliance, establish legal applicability, execute contracts, or replace an audit. Implement controls and obtain scope-specific review.

limitations: Exploratory analysis only. The original recommendation and original requirements are unchanged.
Priority stability counts a finite one-at-a-time sweep; it is not a probability, confidence score or exhaustive sensitivity analysis.

The tradeoff front covers all complete candidates in this finite reviewed catalog, minimizing cost upper bound and operated components while maximizing the ORIGINAL-priority heuristic score. It does not establish real-world optimality or measured architecture quality.

Functional experiments try eligible single/pair edits only: phone login to email/password, payments off, offline support off, full-text search off, or unsupported ML off. They are changed projects, never solutions satisfying the original brief.

Within Decision Lab functional experiments, compliance, infrastructure/residency/provider, tenant isolation, availability, budget, team and timeline are never relaxed. A usable hypothetical result is not legal, security or production approval.
No user assertion authenticates vendor/tenant evidence. Missing contracts, capacity calibration and independent review remain unresolved.

engine_evaluations counts top-level scenario trials; the baseline recommendation may additionally evaluate one separately labeled budget proposal. Budget proposals are outside the functional-experiment sweep and never change the baseline brief.
